key_insight: STROKE shows that a few simple, oriented rectangular occlusions can effectively fool image classifiers without access to their internal workings. The paper reports high attack success with low query counts at nominal 1–2% area settings.
problem_solved: Testing image classifiers with black-box adversarial attacks can require many model queries. STROKE addresses the challenge of finding effective, small-area occlusions using only model scores.
method: Construct sparse perturbations from simple, oriented rectangular occlusions.
Use a lightweight greedy add-and-refine procedure to optimize the occlusions based on model scores.
Evaluate attack success and query counts across diverse image classifiers, including comparisons with existing patch-based attacks.
impact: STROKE offers practitioners a query-efficient way to probe classifier vulnerability to small structural occlusions. Its reported results highlight that limited-area perturbations can still pose a substantial robustness challenge.

paper_title: STROKE: Simple Sparse Structural Occlusions for Black-Box Adversarial Attacks
paper_authors: Ankit Gupta, Akshat Pandya, Paul Lin, Christoph Adami, Emily Dolson
